name: Timeline
statusNote: Alpha, and in transition: list semantics (ol/li) sit behind the primer_react_timeline_list_semantics feature flag, so by default the timeline is still made of divs. Actions and Avatar are recent additions.
summary: A vertical sequence of events joined by a 2px line: each item has a round badge (an icon on a coloured disc) on the line, body text beside it, optional trailing actions and an optional avatar in the left gutter; a break marks a gap in time. Use it for activity feeds and histories; use a plain list when the items are not ordered in time.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Timeline.Item and Timeline.Break children, in display order.

inputs.name: clipSidebar
inputs.description: Trim the line so it does not run past the first item's badge (start), the last item's bottom padding (end), or both; true means both.

inputs.name: condensed
inputs.description: Per item: a compact row with a bare 16px icon in place of the disc, for minor events.

inputs.name: badgeVariant
inputs.description: Per badge: an emphasis-coloured disc with an onEmphasis icon; with none, a muted disc and a muted icon.

inputs.name: badgeIcon
inputs.description: Per item: the octicon inside Timeline.Badge (16px by convention).

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Per item: Timeline.Body, the event text.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.description: Per item: Timeline.Actions, controls at the item's trailing end (under the body when the timeline is narrower than 480px).

inputs.name: avatar
inputs.description: Per item: Timeline.Avatar, an actor avatar placed in the gutter 72px left of the line, centred on the badge.

anatomy.name: Timeline
anatomy.description: A column of items with no padding or margin; it is the inline-size query container for the narrow layout.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: A row (badge, body, actions) inset 16px from the timeline's left edge, with 16px block padding.

anatomy.name: Line
anatomy.description: A 2px vertical bar in --borderColor-muted along each item's left edge, full item height; consecutive items join into one line.

anatomy.name: Badge
anatomy.description: A 32px disc centred on the line with a 2px --bgColor-default ring that cuts the line around it; the icon centred inside.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.description: The event text in body-medium size and --fgColor-muted, filling the row, 8px after the badge.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.description: A row of controls 8px apart, pushed to the trailing end, at least 32px tall so it centres on the badge.

anatomy.name: Avatar
anatomy.description: An absolutely placed actor avatar in the left gutter, vertically centred on the badge, above the line.

anatomy.name: Break
anatomy.description: A 24px band in --bgColor-default with a 4px --borderColor-default rule along its top, spanning the timeline's full width and covering the line.

variants.value: accent | success | attention | severe | danger | done | open | closed | sponsors

variants.description: 4px top padding and none below (16px on the last item); the badge is a 16px-tall, borderless --bgColor-default patch with 8px above and below, its icon --fgColor-muted whatever the variant.

layout.text: Each item is a flex row inset 16px from the timeline's left edge with 16px top and bottom padding; the line is a 2px bar at the item's left edge spanning its full height, so adjacent items draw one continuous line.

The badge is a 32px circle shifted 15px left so its centre sits on the line's centre (1px in), with 8px between it and the body; it never shrinks, clips its content, and sits above the line. Its 2px ring in --bgColor-default leaves a gap in the line around the disc.
The body fills the remaining width (flex auto, min-width 0 so long content wraps instead of overflowing) and starts 5px down (4px + 1px) so its first 21px line centres on the 32px badge.
Actions sit at the row's trailing end (margin-left auto), top-aligned, never shrinking, at least 32px tall with their content centred, 8px apart.

The avatar is positioned 72px (40 + 32) left of the line and centred vertically on the badge: its centre is 32px below the item top (16px padding + half the badge), 20px for a condensed item, 16px for a clipped first item.

A condensed item has 4px top padding and no bottom padding (16px when it is the last item); its badge is 16px tall (still 32px wide), borderless, in --bgColor-default with 8px above and below, so the badge wrapper is still 32px tall.

A break is a 24px band with a 4px --borderColor-default top border, painted in --bgColor-default above the line, starting at the timeline's left edge (not inset); it overlaps the next item by 16px (12px when the next item is condensed).

clipSidebar start removes the first item's top padding, so the line starts at its badge; on a condensed first item the line starts 12px down. clipSidebar end removes the last item's bottom padding, so the line ends at its content; on a condensed last item the line is 12px long.
When the timeline is narrower than 480px, each item becomes a two-column grid (badge | body) and the actions move to a second row under the body, start-aligned, 8px below it, with no minimum height.

states.text: Static: the line is --borderColor-muted, body text --fgColor-muted, and the badge colours follow its variant. Timeline has no hover, focus or selection of its own; controls in Actions carry theirs.

behaviour.text: With the primer_react_timeline_list_semantics flag on, the timeline renders as an ol with role list, items as li and a break as an li with role presentation; with it off (the default) all of them are divs.
Timeline.Badge wraps the badge in a relatively positioned wrapper that lifts it above the line; the badge itself takes any extra props.

accessibility.role: list (behind a feature flag; otherwise generic)
keyboard: Not focusable; Tab moves through links and controls in the bodies and actions in document order.
semantics: With list semantics on, the list announces its item count and each item's position; breaks are hidden from that count (role presentation).
role=list is set explicitly because Safari drops list semantics from a list styled with list-style: none.
A badge icon that carries meaning (merged, closed) needs a text alternative; the timeline supplies none.

notes.text: The narrow layout is a CSS container query on the timeline's own inline size (below 480px), not the viewport. A native build must know the timeline's width before laying out items, since it decides whether actions share the body's row or take a row of their own, which changes every item's height.

container-type: inline-size gives the timeline inline-size containment: its width cannot come from its content. In a shrink-to-fit parent (inline-block, a flex item sized by content, a float) it collapses to zero width. A native port should size the timeline from its parent, never from its items.

The line is not one stroke: it is each item's own 2px bar, and the badge's 2px --bgColor-default ring and the condensed badge's --bgColor-default fill paint over it. Draw the line first, then the badges, on the timeline's actual background; on a surface other than --bgColor-default the ring shows as a visible halo.
A condensed item ignores the badge variant: its rule sets the icon to --fgColor-muted and the fill to --bgColor-default and outranks the variant rules, which sit inside :where().

The avatar is absolutely positioned 72px left of the line, which is itself 16px inside the timeline, so the avatar starts 56px outside the timeline's left edge; the timeline's parent must leave that gutter, since nothing in the component reserves it.

The break's tighter overlap before a condensed item uses :has(+ [data-condensed]), a look-ahead at the next sibling. A native build decides it while iterating the children: check the next item's condensed flag before placing the break.
The 2px line, 32px badge, -15px badge offset, 16px condensed badge height, 1px body nudge and 480px container breakpoint are literals; the badge radius is 50%.

An uncoloured badge fills with --timelineBadge-bgColor (an alias of --bgColor-muted), not a bgColor token directly; a TODO beside it says the migration to that token was uncertain, so do not substitute --bgColor-muted, which themes may later bind apart.
